headline: A rough night on Wall Street dragged US tech names lower, PLS.AX smashed 3.75% on lithium woes, and the Panthers delivered the NRL's most one-sided result of the season.

movers.name: Pilbara Minerals
movers.note: Pilbara had a tough session today, falling 3.75% to $5.91. Lithium prices remain under pressure as top Chinese lithium miners have seen their stocks crash, signalling the global lithium rally has stalled. With no near-term catalyst to reverse the oversupply story, sentiment on ASX lithium stocks like PLS stays soft.

movers.name: Microsoft
movers.note: Microsoft dropped 2.66% last night in a broad tech sell-off on the NASDAQ (which fell 4.18%). No single company-specific news drove the move — the whole market took a hit, and as one of the largest tech stocks, Microsoft copped more than most. It's now sitting at a loss overall in the portfolio.

movers.name: Global X Artificial Intelligence ETF
movers.note: GXAI fell 1.74% today to $18.05, tracking weakness in global AI-linked tech stocks. The ETF holds a basket of AI companies, many of which are listed on US exchanges, so last night's NASDAQ sell-off fed through into today's ASX price. Motley Fool still backs GXAI as a long-term AI growth pick, but short-term it's caught in the crossfire.

movers.name: Take-Two Interactive
movers.note: Take-Two slipped 1.04% last night, mostly dragged along with the broader tech sell-off rather than any company-specific bad news. The only TTWO news doing the rounds is retrospective praise for GTA V — no red flags, just market noise.

movers.name: Alphabet Inc. (Google)
movers.note: Google fell about 0.95% last night as part of the wider NASDAQ tumble. No company-specific news drove the drop — it's a market-wide tech pullback. Google remains well in the green overall for the portfolio, up 26.55% since purchase.

movers.name: Vanguard FTSE Emerging Markets ETF
movers.note: VGE dipped 0.94% today to $92.03. Emerging markets felt the pinch as the Aussie dollar fell against the USD, which can amplify moves in globally-exposed ETFs. Broader risk-off sentiment didn't help either.

movers.name: BetaShares Global Energy Companies ETF
movers.note: FUEL slipped 0.8% today to $8.70, in line with crude oil falling 2.69% last night (from $93.04 to $90.54 a barrel). When oil prices drop, energy company earnings expectations follow, and that feeds straight into this ETF.

movers.name: Vanguard US Total Market Shares ETF
movers.note: VTS nudged up 0.31% today to $521.82, a modest positive given last night's heavy US sell-off. The ASX-listed version can lag or diverge slightly from the US session due to currency moves and timing — a small win in an otherwise red day.

movers.name: Vanguard Diversified High Growth ETF
movers.note: VDHG held steady with a tiny 0.12% gain today to $75.95. Its broad diversification across asset classes (Aussie and international shares, bonds) cushioned it from the worst of the tech-driven sell-off. This is exactly what a diversified fund is supposed to do.

watch_today.title: PLS.AX — lithium pain continues
watch_today.detail: Pilbara fell 3.75% today and is now down 12.31% from what you paid. Chinese lithium miners are crashing as the global lithium rally collapses on oversupply. There's no clear floor yet — if you're still comfortable with the thesis long-term, hold, but it's worth reviewing your conviction here.

watch_today.title: MSFT — big night of losses, watch the recovery
watch_today.detail: Microsoft dropped 2.66% last night as the NASDAQ cratered 4.18% — the worst session in a while. MSFT is now sitting at a loss in your portfolio (-5.97%). US markets haven't opened yet tonight — if the sell-off continues, expect further pressure. No company-specific bad news, just market-wide pain.

watch_today.title: GXAI.AX — AI ETF caught in tech wreckage
watch_today.detail: GXAI fell 1.74% today and is down 5.15% overall. The AI regulation debate in the US is heating up (Trump's new executive order could change how OpenAI, Google and Anthropic launch models), which adds uncertainty to AI stocks. Motley Fool still likes it for long-term growth. Hold unless you see more regulatory shock.

watch_today.title: NASDAQ down 4.18% last night — brace for US open tonight
watch_today.detail: Last night's NASDAQ close was brutal, falling over 1,121 points (4.18%). The S&P 500 dropped 2.64%. Watch tonight's US open (from ~11:30 PM AEST) — if the slide continues, your GOOG, MSFT, and TTWO positions will feel more heat tomorrow morning.

watch_today.title: GOOG — holding up well despite the carnage
watch_today.detail: Google only fell 0.95% last night, outperforming the broader NASDAQ drop of 4.18%. It's still your best-performing holding at +26.55%. Nothing to do here — just keep an eye on whether the US AI regulation debate (Trump's new executive order) creates any company-specific headwinds.

watch_today.title: Trump's AI executive order — watch for impact on GOOG and GXAI
watch_today.detail: A new US executive order is reportedly set to change how companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic can launch AI models — essentially shifting power from private companies to government oversight. This could slow AI product releases and weigh on AI-linked stocks. Worth watching how GOOG and GXAI respond over the coming week.

markets.summary: Last night on Wall Street was a shocker — the NASDAQ dropped 4.18% and the S&P 500 fell 2.64%, dragged down by a broad tech sell-off. Crude oil slid 2.69% to $90.54 a barrel, and gold dropped 2.47% to $4,365. The Aussie dollar also fell, dropping from 71.3 US cents to 70.5 US cents. Closer to home, the ASX 200 closed down 0.7% today at 8,625 — a softer but far less dramatic pullback than what Wall Street suffered.

indicators.name: ASX 200
indicators.note: Closed down 0.7% today — soft but orderly compared to Wall Street's chaos.

indicators.name: S&P 500
indicators.note: Last night's session: dropped 2.64%, a significant broad market sell-off.

indicators.name: NASDAQ Composite
indicators.note: Last night's session: fell 4.18% — worst of the major indices, tech took the brunt.

indicators.name: Crude Oil (WTI)
indicators.note: Oil fell 2.69% last night, dragging energy stocks and FUEL.AX lower.

indicators.name: Gold
indicators.note: Gold dropped 2.47% — unusual to see it fall in a risk-off day, suggests broad liquidation.

indicators.name: AUD/USD
indicators.note: The Aussie slipped to 70.5 US cents — makes your US holdings worth slightly less in AUD terms.

politics.summary: No Australian political stories made the feed today — parliament is likely in recess and it was a quiet Sunday on the domestic political front. Nothing to report that would affect your portfolio.

ai.summary: The big AI story this weekend is US regulatory politics — Trump has signed or is circulating a new executive order that could fundamentally change how AI companies like OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch products. The debate about who controls AI — governments or private companies — is intensifying, and that matters for your GOOG and GXAI holdings.

stories.title: Trump's new AI order could change how OpenAI, Google, and Anthropic launch models
stories.why_it_matters: A new Trump executive order is set to reshape how AI companies can release new models — reportedly giving the federal government more say over what gets launched and when. This directly affects Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic, who have all been moving fast on AI product releases. More government control could slow the pace of AI innovation and weigh on AI-linked stocks like GOOG and your GXAI.AX ETF. The order reflects Trump's view that AI is too strategically important to leave entirely to private companies.

stories.title: OpenAI and the White House have competing visions for regulating artificial intelligence
stories.why_it_matters: OpenAI and the White House are publicly at odds on what AI regulation should look like. OpenAI wants a lighter-touch framework that lets them keep moving fast; the White House wants more oversight and potentially government sign-off on major model launches. This tug-of-war creates uncertainty for investors in AI companies — regulations that slow product cycles could dent revenue growth expectations.

stories.title: Federal AI Regulation Bill Freezes State Consumer Protections for Three Years, Sparks Revolt
stories.why_it_matters: A new US federal AI bill would freeze state-level consumer protection laws around AI for three years — meaning individual US states couldn't introduce their own AI rules while Congress figures out a national framework. This has sparked a backlash from state governments and consumer advocates. For investors, a federal-only approach could create a more predictable (if lighter) regulatory environment for big AI companies like Google and Microsoft.

stories.title: Tencent Hires Former OpenAI Researcher Yao Shunyu As Chief AI Scientist In AGI Push
stories.why_it_matters: China's Tencent has poached Yao Shunyu — a prominent researcher who was at OpenAI — and made him Chief AI Scientist, as part of a push toward AGI (Artificial General Intelligence, meaning AI that can do pretty much anything a human can). This signals that the US-China AI race is intensifying at the talent level, not just the hardware or model level. For long-term AI investors, more Chinese competition could pressure the US companies that dominate your GXAI ETF.

sport.summary: The NRL's Round 14 wrapped up with some wild results — Penrith absolutely demolished Wests Tigers 68-0, and the Gold Coast Titans pulled off a shock win over the Broncos at Suncorp. In AFL, Fremantle smashed North Melbourne by a record margin. Nick Kyrgios has also confirmed another tennis comeback ahead of Wimbledon.

stories.title: 'Almost cruel': Panthers humiliate Tigers 68-0 in record thrashing
stories.why_it_matters: Penrith ran riot over Wests Tigers 68-0 at CommBank Stadium — the biggest win of the NRL season so far. Nathan Cleary was in full flight and reportedly used the performance to fire an Origin (State of Origin) warning to rivals. The Tigers were booed off by their own fans. Fox Sports described the performance as 'almost cruel', and the result raises serious questions about whether the Tigers have any real answers this season. NSW Blues selectors will be sweating on any Panthers players who picked up knocks.

stories.title: Broncos rocked as Titans score Suncorp miracle — Reece Walsh exposed
stories.why_it_matters: The Gold Coast Titans pulled off a stunning 28-23 upset over the Broncos at Suncorp Stadium on Saturday night. Fox Sports reported Reece Walsh had a night to forget and described the result as a 'nightmare' for Broncos coach Michael Maguire. The Titans have now beaten the home side at Suncorp, which is a big statement given the Broncos' form this year. Queensland fans on the Gold Coast will be loving it.

stories.title: Dolphins thrash Cowboys 40-14 with five straight wins — NQ gun faces ban
stories.why_it_matters: The Dolphins demolished North Queensland Cowboys 40-14, claiming their fifth consecutive win and cementing themselves as genuine finals contenders. Origin stars were on show for the Dolphins. Meanwhile, a Cowboys player is set to learn his fate after his third high-tackle offence — a third strike typically means a suspension under NRL judiciary rules, which would be a significant blow for North Queensland's season.

stories.title: Dockers thrash North Melbourne by record margin — Clarkson 'bitterly disappointed'
stories.why_it_matters: Fremantle beat North Melbourne by a record margin, according to ESPN, handing North coach Chris Clarkson his biggest loss as a coach. Nine.com.au reported Clarkson was 'bitterly disappointed' after the shellacking. The Dockers are on a roll and building a case as one of the competition's form sides, while North Melbourne's season is in serious trouble early.

stories.title: Nick Kyrgios confirms tennis comeback — Wimbledon in his sights
stories.why_it_matters: Nick Kyrgios has officially confirmed another comeback to professional tennis, with Wimbledon reportedly in his plans. Kyrgios has had a turbulent few years with injuries and personal issues. No details yet on which lead-up tournaments he'll play, but the confirmation alone will generate massive media interest ahead of the grasscourt Grand Slam.
